summary: A Spanish-built light on Vieques, begun in 1895 and lit in 1896: seven keeper stints, a 1931 rescue, automation in 1949 and a museum that has opened and closed.

structures.note: Begun 1895, finished 1896 (1901 report). 27 ft from the base (1901 report); the 1976 nomination gives 50 ft including the lantern

access.note: Sources disagree. The 1976 nomination records restricted access. LighthouseFriends says the museum was closed to the public by 2005, though its visitor notes list the grounds and dwelling as open; its writer found the grounds closed on a 2009 visit. A tourism page calls it a museum. Check locally before any visit.

events.note: Begun by the Spanish government (1901 report)
Began operating 1 June 1896 (EnciclopediaPR); commenced operation in 1896 (LighthouseFriends)
Finished 1896 by the Spanish, at a cost of 14,500 pesos (1901 report)
Lighthouse Board directed to take charge of Porto Rico's lights, 1 May 1900
Keeper Cayetano Valle commended for rescuing two men near the light; the Bulletin dates the rescue 17 August
1944 alterations: former pantry became a power plant, dining room a battery room (nomination). The brick roof was rebuilt in reinforced concrete in the 1940s (year not given)
Converted to an unattended automatic light and boarded up
A caretaker began living in the dwelling in the 1960s (decade only)
Restored in 1992; municipal purchase per EnciclopediaPR
Opened as a museum on 12 October 1992 (LighthouseFriends)
Hurricane Georges; the building was restored again afterwards
Closed to the public after water damage (LighthouseFriends)
Reinaugurated in 2015 (EnciclopediaPR); current opening not confirmed by the sources read

corrections.why: The HAER data pages are headed 'HAER No. PR-15'. The Library of Congress item pr0034 is a catalogue identifier, not the HAER number.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1901 report says begun 1895 and finished 1896. The nomination's description says built in 1895 and its specific dates say 1896. EnciclopediaPR says construction dated from the year before the light began operating on 1 June 1896. The record's 1896 is the finishing and first-lit year.

The 1901 report gives the tower as 27 ft from its base; the nomination gives 50 ft including the lantern. The difference is the measure used. The record's 10 m (about 33 ft) is a Wikidata figure and is not cited here.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: location on the island. The 1901 report says the northerly shore (it also calls the island Crab Island); the NRHP nomination, the HAER data pages and the USLHS place record say the western shore; EnciclopediaPR says west of the port of Isabel II; LighthouseFriends says just east of Isabella Segunda. The story states all four. Unresolved: the designer (the 1976 nomination gives Eng. Jose M. Sanz; EnciclopediaPR gives Francisco de Albacete). Unresolved: ownership (LighthouseFriends and HAER name the Coast Guard, HAER also names the Department of Commerce; EnciclopediaPR says the municipal government bought it in 1992). Unresolved: current access. LighthouseFriends' visitor notes say 'Grounds/dwelling open' while the same page says the museum was closed and its 2009 writer found the grounds closed. Verify before anyone visits. Range: the 1901 report gives a shorter range than the nomination's 8 miles (its scan text reads 7i miles, which we did not turn into a number); the record's 7.5 nm was removed because the source does not say nautical miles and the figure is unread. The 1901 report also says in one passage that the Porto Rican service was under the Board from 'May 1, 1899' (scan text 'Mav 1, 1899'); its Porto Rico section and the 1900 report say 1 May 1900, which the story follows. The USLHS place record gives an 1885 establishment, tower and lens; no source read supports 1885, so it is not used. The station record's HAER PR-34 is corrected to PR-15 (see corrections). The NRHP listing year 1977 was not checked on the register itself, so no nrhp_listed event is given. Roster matched by position (0.42 km, the only USLHS place there) and cited to the place page; the USLHS spans are quoted as printed. The roster lists the Coffie stint (1932-1933) that LighthouseFriends does not list. LighthouseFriends is cited for facts; quotations kept to short phrases. The vieques.com page credits Don Juan Puig Cerber with the 1895 construction; no record supports that, so it is not used. A newspapers.py search for 'Punta Mulas' returned 1896 to 1923 hits in Gazeta de Puerto-Rico and El Imparcial; the page fetch timed out, so none were read. Wikipedia was used only as a lead. The HAER data pages repeat the nomination's wording almost word for word; they are not independent evidence for the building.
